title: Follow the Water
intro: Roads that keep a river or a lake in the passenger window. Good for slow afternoons, and for anyone who likes to pull over just to watch the water move.

title: Higher Ground
intro: Switchbacks and long ridge views. Several of these close or change with the seasons, so check with the managing agency before you go.

title: Edge of the Map
intro: Where the land runs out. Lighthouses, bridges over coves, and the particular light you only get near open water.

title: Desert Light
intro: Red rock and open sky. Carry water, watch the fuel gauge, and plan around the heat of the day.

title: Small Towns, Long Views
intro: Roads where the stops are the point. Diners, courthouses, covered bridges, and the old highways that tied them together.

title: Classic Drives
intro: Some of America's best-known drives were never designated scenic byways. These are here because people drive across the country for them. Route lines come from OpenStreetMap or the managing agency, and each is labelled as a classic drive rather than a byway.
